instructions: Bloom the Cajun Spice in the Oil with the Garlic and deglaze with the Vinegar; let cool.
Drain the Tofu and cut into slices; add to a vac bag and coat in the Oil and Spice.
Seal in the bag for 24 h.

recipes.notes:
Storage: Two kinds of bag: 4 × ~8½ lb DONBURI ONION SAUCE (vegan) and 4 × ~9 lb DONBURI BEEF. Blast chill, vac bag, lay flat, refrigerate at 4°C (40°F) or below. At Rexdale, boil the sauce, then fold in the Beef and heat to 74°C (165°F) without boiling.
Two bags, not one: the Beef is roasted and chilled and never simmered at Bloor, so it is cooked hard only once. At Rexdale it just warms through in sauce that has already boiled. The beef method is borrowed from Ginger Beef (Jason's card, 2026-11-05), which is still a draft that hasn't been test-batched, so test this on one batch first.
The pan juices go in the beef bags, not the sauce, so the Onion Sauce stays vegan and can be shared with the vegan card.
No mirin or sake: both contain alcohol, so sugar and rice vinegar give the sweet-sharp balance and the batch stays halal.
Kombu–shiitake broth instead of bonito (fish) broth: no fish allergen, and the same sauce works for the vegan card.
Kombu is optional: buy it as dasima (다시마) at a Korean market. A 2 lb bag keeps a year or more sealed and dry and covers about 7 batches; buy the Dried Shiitake there too. Without it, use 200 g Dried Shiitake (50 g more); the sauce is a little flatter but fine.
Served over rice: in CODEX, add Plain Rice (Rexdale) under Served with (role starch, made at Rex). The rice is not on this card.
Same-day shortcut: make the Broth and Onion Sauce sections 1.15× and bag one extra sauce bag of about 4½ lbs labelled VEGAN for the Mushroom Donburi; the vegan card then skips its broth and sauce steps.
Sesame seeds on the side are optional and add Sesame. A soft egg on top is traditional and adds Eggs — leave both off the default plate.
Yield math: roasting thin slices loses about 40%, so 1 case (27 kg / 59½ lbs) gives about 36 lbs of beef. The Onion Sauce is about 34 lbs (about 14 lbs simmered onion, about 20 lbs sauce). That is about 70 lbs, or 170 portions of about 6½ oz (about 3.4 oz beef + 3.2 oz sauce). Weigh the first batch's bags and note them.
Cost: the beef is COST_DB's own outside round case price ($420.93 / 27 kg). Rice adds about $0.09 a plate.

ingredients.name: Halal Beef Outside Round, raw (1 case; ~36 lbs once roasted)
Green Onion, sliced (packed on the side)

instructions: Slice the Beef: firm the roasts in the freezer until stiff but not frozen solid (about 1–2 h), then slice about 3 mm (⅛") thick across the grain on the meat slicer. Trim off gristle and heavy fat as you go. Keep the sliced Beef cold.

Marinate: in bus bins, whisk the marinade Soy Sauce, Oil, Sugar, Ginger and Cornstarch. Add the Beef and toss until every piece is coated — the cornstarch coating is what keeps the thin slices tender through bagging and reheating. Cover, label and refrigerate at least 2 hours — overnight is best.

Make the Onion Sauce first, before any Beef is out, with clean pots and tools — it is vegan. Make the broth: in a large stock pot, soak Kombu and Dried Shiitake in the Water for 30 min (or overnight in the fridge). Heat slowly over medium heat. Lift the Kombu out just before the water boils — boiled kombu turns slimy and bitter. Simmer the Shiitake 10 min, then strain. Slice the Shiitake thin and keep it. Expect about 7 L of broth. No Kombu? Use 200 g Dried Shiitake and skip the Kombu.

Add the sauce Soy Sauce, Sugar, Rice Vinegar and Ginger to the broth and stir until the Sugar dissolves. Add the Onions and the sliced Shiitake (split between two pots if one won't hold it). Simmer until the Onions are soft but still hold their shape, 20–25 min. Taste: it should be sweet-salty, like a thin teriyaki.
Whisk the sauce Cornstarch into 300 mL cold water, stir it into the simmering pot and cook 2 min. Keep it loose: over rice the sauce should soak in, not sit on top like gravy.

Bag the Onion Sauce: blast chill, then vac bag in 4 bags of about 8½ lbs, spreading the Onions evenly between them. Lay flat. Label each "DONBURI ONION SAUCE — VEGAN". Wash up before the Beef comes out.

Roast the Beef: spread it on parchment-lined sheet pans in a single layer — shake off excess marinade and don't crowd the pans, or it steams and goes grey instead of browning. Roast at 230°C (450°F) until browned at the edges and no pink remains, 12–15 min per load, rotating pans halfway. Stop there: it is heated again at Rexdale. Pour the pan juices into a container, skim the fat and keep them. Repeat until it is all roasted.

Bag the Beef: blast chill it straight from the pans — don't simmer or fold it into anything. Vac bag in 4 bags of about 9 lbs, splitting the skimmed pan juices evenly between them so the Beef stays moist. Lay the bags flat so the slices don't set into a slab. Label each "DONBURI BEEF". Pack the Green Onion in a deli container and label it for Rexdale.
FOR HALAL: all beef is halal and the sauce has no alcohol (no mirin or sake) — this batch serves Halal as-is.
FOR VEGAN: use the Mushroom Donburi card (Mushroom_Donburi_Vegan). The Onion Sauce is vegan, so a spare sauce bag can go with it (see Notes).

AT REXDALE: one sauce bag + one beef bag makes about 42 portions. Bring the Onion Sauce to a boil in a pot first. Flex the beef bag to break up the slices, add the Beef and its juices, fold gently and heat to 74°C (165°F), about 5 min — once the Beef is in, don't boil it. Put about 6 oz Plain Rice in the bowl, ladle about 6½ oz over it and top with Green Onion. If plates are made ahead, keep rice and topping apart until service.

ingredients.name: Halal Ground Beef (raw, to be browned)

instructions: Cook Halal Ground Beef in a large pot on the gas burner over medium-high heat, breaking it into small pieces as it cooks. Cook until no pink remains and some browning develops. Drain off cooking liquid and fat into a separate container; let fat separate.
Skim fat from drained liquid and add 1 cup of rendered beef fat back to the pot. Sauté Onions and Crushed Garlic in the beef fat until softened and lightly coloured.
Stir in Nacho Spice Mix and cook 1–2 minutes. Add pre-steamed Carrots, Celery, and Peppers and sauté 5–10 minutes.
Add cooked Beef back to the pot. Stir to combine; if mixture is dry, add some of the reserved Beef jus to loosen.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Cool in hotel pans and vac bag in 10 lb bags.
Trim Beef and cut into 1" cubes
Roast beef cubes until browned at 425°F; meanwhile simmer beef offcuts in 10L water with Carrot, Onion, and Celery scraps to make a stock. Strain and reserve.
Add browned beef to a deep hotel or pot with a few ladles of stock. Braise covered at 325°F for 2–2.5 hours until tender.
Sauté Onions until soft. Add Crushed Tomato and cook 10 minutes.
Add Diced Carrot and Diced Parsnip with remaining stock. Simmer until veg is tender, ~20–30 minutes.

Make a roux to thicken: in a separate pan, melt butter or use a ladle of beef fat skimmed from the braising liquid. Whisk in Flour and cook 2–3 minutes until the raw flour smell is gone. Whisk in warm stock gradually until smooth, then stir the roux into the stew. Simmer 5 minutes.
Add braised beef and Frozen Peas. Stir gently to combine. Adjust seasoning.
Cool in hotels. Vac bag in 10 lb bags. Label and date.

ingredients.name: Halal Beef Outside Round, raw, cubed

instructions: Trim Beef outside round, cube into bite-sized pieces. Reserve scraps and bones; make a beef stock from scraps, strain and set aside.
Roast beef cubes at 450°F to develop colour, then add reserved broth and braise covered until tender.
Steam Carrots 20 minutes until just tender; set aside. Sauté Onions, Celery, and Peppers together until softened. Add pre-steamed Carrots and Crushed Tomato; cook to combine flavours.
Melt Butter and whisk in Flour to make a roux. Gradually whisk in Beef Braising Liquid until smooth. Simmer to thicken.
Combine sautéed veg, braised beef, and thickened sauce. Transfer to hotel pans and cool in blast chiller.
Once cooled, fold in Sour Cream and stir to combine. Vac bag in 10 lb bags.

recipes.notes:
Storage: Blast chill; vac bag in 10 lb bags; refrigerate at 4°C (40°F) or below and send to Rexdale cold. Reheat to 74°C (165°F), stirring, on gentle heat. Serve over pasta.
Allergens: Nightshades (Crushed Tomatoes, Tomato Paste) only. The vegan batch is its own recipe, Vegan Bolognese, with its own allergens (from the Vegan Meat Replacement).
No wine and no milk: wine is left out so the batch serves Halal, and milk so No-Dairy residents can eat it.
Pasta is not included. Serve about 8 oz of sauce over 6–8 oz of cooked pasta; Rexdale cooks the pasta on site.
Changes from Beef Lasagna Sauce (CODEX): no peppers; the carrots are finely diced and sweated, not steamed; the tomato paste is cooked until it darkens; nutmeg, basil and bay are added; and the sauce simmers about 90 min in all, with the beef in for the last 45. The 3 L for the Vegan Bolognese comes out of the same pot before the beef goes in.
Yield math: about 32 lbs of soffritto cooks down to about 24 lbs. With the garlic, paste, tomatoes and water that is about 70 lbs, and about 9 lbs simmers off, leaving about 61 lbs of sauce. The vegan pull takes about 7 lbs (3 L), leaving about 54 lbs. 40 lbs of raw beef browns and drains to about 29 lbs, which makes about 83 lbs (165 portions at 8 oz). Evaporation depends on the pot, so weigh the first batch and note the result.
Split from the combined Bolognese card (2026-10-29) on 2026-11-09 so DOOR reads the beef line's allergens on their own.

ingredients.name: Halal Ground Beef (raw, to be browned)

instructions: Prep the Soffritto: finely dice the Onions, Carrots and Celery — pulse in the food processor in small loads so the pieces are small and even (about the size of a lentil), but don't purée them. Keep the Onions in their own bin; Carrots and Celery can share one.

Brown the Beef in batches in a large pot over medium-high heat, breaking it into small pieces as it cooks. Don't crowd the pot — it should sizzle, not stew. Cook until no pink remains, it reaches 71°C (160°F) and some browning develops. Drain the fat into a separate container (never down the drain) and set the Beef aside, covered. Use this pot and these tools for Beef only.

In a clean large stock pot (split everything between two pots if one won't hold it), heat the Oil over medium heat. Add the Onions and a pinch of the Salt and cook 10 min until soft. Add the Carrots and Celery and cook, stirring often, until everything is soft and sweet with no colour, 20–25 min.

Add the Garlic and cook 2–3 min until fragrant. Add the Tomato Paste and stir constantly for about 5 min, until it darkens to brick red and starts to catch on the bottom — scrape it up as you go. This is where the depth comes from.

Add the Crushed Tomatoes, Water, Oregano, Basil, Bay Leaves, Nutmeg, Sugar, Salt (200 g) and Black Pepper. Bring to a simmer, then cook gently for 45 min, stirring from the bottom often (it spits and catches). The pot is still vegan at this point: keep beef tongs, spoons and drained fat away from it.

FOR THE VEGAN BOLOGNESE: before any Beef goes in, move 3 L of the sauce with a clean ladle into a clean pot and hand it to whoever is making the Vegan Bolognese (see that recipe). Keep beef tongs, spoons and drained fat away from it.

Add the browned Beef to the remaining sauce. Simmer gently for 45 min more, stirring often, until thick and rich — it should sit on a spoon, not run off it. Loosen with a little water if it gets too thick. Remove the Bay Leaves, taste and adjust the Salt, and bring to 74°C (165°F).
Cool in the blast chiller and vac bag in 10 lb bags — expect about 8 bags (≈ 83 lbs) of Bolognese. The Vegan Bolognese is bagged and labelled on its own.
FOR HALAL: all ground beef is halal — this batch serves Halal as-is.
Season Chicken with Salt and Pepper. Roast at 425°F until internal temp reaches 195°F. Set aside to cool, then chop into bite-sized pieces.

Heat Oil in a large pot. Sauté Crushed Garlic and Minced Ginger with a heavy pinch of salt and a splash of water until fragrant. Add Onions and cook until softened and beginning to colour; stir in Curry Spice Mix.
Add Peppers and Carrots (pre-steamed 20 minutes). Sauté for 5 minutes.
Add Diced Tomatoes and Crushed Tomatoes. Bring to a simmer, stirring regularly.
Stir in Coconut Milk and bring back to heat.
Add chopped Cooked Chicken and stir to combine.
Fold in Cilantro in Oil. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Cool in blast chiller and vac bag in 10 lb bags.

recipes.kitchenNote: Batch makes about 15 lb (20 portions of 12 oz). Rexdale’s vegan line is served 15 portions (about 11.5 lb); about 4 lb extra. Don’t scale the batch down to Rex’s count. (Jason, 2026-11-12)

ingredients.name: Sweet Potatoes, peeled and cubed, steamed

Collard Greens, stems removed, leaves chopped
Cooked Chickpeas — FOR VEGAN ALT (or 1 can per 6 lbs stew)

instructions: Prep all ingredients: peel, cube, and steam Sweet Potatoes and Carrots; wash, de-stem, and chop Collard Greens.
Heat Canola Oil in a large pot. Add Garlic and Ginger with a splash of Water; cook until water has evaporated.
Add Onions and 1 qt Water. Cover and cook until onions are well softened and beginning to colour.
Add more Water, Veg Broth Powder, canned Roasted Red Peppers, and Scotch Bonnets. Stir to combine.
Stir in Tomato Paste with more water as needed to build a base sauce. Add dry spices: Thyme, Black Pepper, Curry Powder, Smoked Paprika, and Garlic/Pepper Seasoning.
Add Fresh Red Bell Peppers and stir to coat.
Add Canned Diced Tomatoes. Bring to heat and simmer 20–30 minutes.
Add steamed Sweet Potatoes and Carrots. Simmer, stirring occasionally, until sweet potatoes are fully cooked and sauce has thickened slightly.
Add Red Wine Vinegar and Coconut Milk. Stir well and adjust seasoning — add more vinegar or salt to taste.
Stir in chopped Collard Greens and allow to wilt into the stew. Add Okra if available.
Cool in hotel pans.

recipes.notes:
Storage: Send hot; hold at 60°C (140°F) or above. Leftovers: blast chill within 2 h (cooked rice grows Bacillus cereus when held warm), refrigerate at 4°C (40°F) or below and reheat once to 74°C (165°F).
Built from Chicken and Mushroom Fried Rice and Arroz Con Pollo: the same rice method and batch, and the same 25 kg chicken case.
Kimchi is store-bought. Its label: Napa Cabbage, Sugar, Salt, Chilli Powder, Ginger, Soy Sauce (Soybean, Water, Wheat, Salt, Fructose, Ethyl Alcohol, Yeast Extract, Stevia, Licorice Extract, Seed Malt, Ethyl Parahydroxybenzoate), Green Onion, Carrot, Garlic. Contains Soy, Wheat. It has no fish sauce or shrimp, so it is vegan.
GLUTEN: the kimchi's own soy sauce contains wheat, so this dish has Gluten even though CONC's soy sauce doesn't. Re-check the allergen line if the kimchi brand changes.
SPICY: the kimchi's chilli makes this mildly spicy, so Spicy is on the allergen line.
HALAL: the kimchi's soy sauce lists ethyl alcohol (a brewing/preservative trace). Ruled fine for halal (Jason, 2026-11-11).
Not used: gochujang (most brands contain wheat and some contain alcohol) and fish sauce (adds Fish).
Same-day shortcut for the vegan card: before the Chicken goes in at step 5, pull enough rice, kimchi base and Peas and Carrots for one 4" hotel with a clean paddle and hand it to the vegan card.
Kimchi amount: one case (4 × 2 L jars). If it tastes flat, add a little more brine, not more Soy Sauce.

ingredients.name: Boneless Halal Chicken Legs, raw (~32 lbs once roasted)
Vegan Kimchi, store-bought, drained and chopped — keep the brine

instructions: Season the Chicken with the Salt and Black Pepper and spread on lined sheet pans in a single layer. Roast at 230°C (450°F) until browned and 74°C (165°F) inside, 30–35 min. Cool slightly, then chop into bite-size pieces.

Rice: in 4 × 6" hotel pans, combine 4 kg Rice and ½ cup Canola Oil per pan and mix well. Add 6 L Water to each, cover, and cook at 230°C (450°F), 100% moisture, fan 2, for 50 min. Uncover and fluff with a paddle so the steam escapes — drier rice fries better and doesn't go mushy.
Kimchi: drain the Kimchi over a container and keep the brine. Chop the Kimchi into about 1 cm (½") pieces.

Kimchi base: heat the Canola Oil in the tilt skillet. Cook the Onion until soft, about 8 min, then add the Garlic for 1 min. Add the chopped Kimchi and cook, stirring, until it softens and the edges start to colour, 8–10 min. Stir in the kimchi brine, Soy Sauce and Sugar and simmer 2 min. Taste: tangy, savoury and mildly spicy.

Combine: fold the fluffed Rice, the kimchi base, the frozen Peas and Carrots and the chopped Chicken together evenly — divide the base by weight so every pan gets the same colour and seasoning. Fill 4" hotels (about 14).
Bake the hotels uncovered at 230°C (450°F), dry heat (0% moisture), for 15–20 min, stirring once halfway, until the top grains are lightly crisped and the centre reads 74°C (165°F).
Finish: drizzle the Sesame Oil over the hotels and toss, then scatter the Green Onions on top. Cover and send hot.
FOR HALAL: all chicken is halal and the alcohol trace in the kimchi's soy sauce is fine for halal (Jason, 2026-11-11) — this batch serves Halal as-is.
FOR VEGAN: use the Kimchi Fried Rice (Vegan) card (Kimchi_Fried_Rice_Vegan).

recipes.notes:
Storage: Send hot; hold at 60°C (140°F) or above. Leftovers: blast chill within 2 h (cooked rice grows Bacillus cereus when held warm), refrigerate at 4°C (40°F) or below and reheat once to 74°C (165°F).
The vegan alternative to Kimchi Chicken Fried Rice (Kimchi_Chicken_Fried_Rice_Main): the same kimchi base, built small so it can be cooked on its own. Vegan Chik'n as on the Arroz Con Pollo card.
Same-day shortcut: take one 4" hotel of the chicken card's combined rice, kimchi base and Peas and Carrots, pulled BEFORE its Chicken goes in (clean paddle), and skip steps 1 and 3 here.
Kimchi is store-bought. Its label: Napa Cabbage, Sugar, Salt, Chilli Powder, Ginger, Soy Sauce (Soybean, Water, Wheat, Salt, Fructose, Ethyl Alcohol, Yeast Extract, Stevia, Licorice Extract, Seed Malt, Ethyl Parahydroxybenzoate), Green Onion, Carrot, Garlic. Contains Soy, Wheat. It has no fish sauce or shrimp, so it is vegan.
GLUTEN: the kimchi's own soy sauce contains wheat, so this dish has Gluten even though CONC's soy sauce doesn't. Re-check the allergen line if the kimchi brand changes.
SPICY: the kimchi's chilli makes this mildly spicy, so Spicy is on the allergen line.
Vegan Chik'n is Gardein: it contains wheat and soy (Jason, 2026-11-12), so Gluten and Soy both name it. Gluten-free residents can't have this dish even without the kimchi.
Not used: gochujang (most brands contain wheat and some contain alcohol) and fish sauce (adds Fish).
Less Soy Sauce than the chicken card's share (120 mL, not 190 mL): the Vegan Chik'n is already salted. Taste before adding more. If you use the same-day shortcut, the rice is already seasoned: add no Soy Sauce.
To scale: about 1 L (½ jar) kimchi, 1.5 kg rice and 5 lbs Vegan Chik'n per 15 portions.
Cost: kimchi is $92.01 a case of 4 × 2 L jars ($11.50 a litre; Jason, 2026-11-11). It isn't in CODEX's COST_DB yet.

instructions: Use clean pots, boards and tongs that have not touched beef. Make the broth: soak Kombu and Dried Shiitake in the Water for 30 min. Heat slowly; lift the Kombu out just before it boils. Simmer the Shiitake 10 min, then strain. Slice the Shiitake thin and keep it. Expect about 1 L of broth. No Kombu? Use 50 g Dried Shiitake and skip the Kombu.

Toss the Mushrooms with two-thirds of the Oil and half the Salt; toss the Tofu with the rest. Spread each in a single layer on lined sheet pans — don't crowd them. Roast at 220°C (425°F) until the Mushrooms are browned and their liquid has cooked off and the Tofu edges are golden, 20–25 min. Roasting first keeps the bags from going watery.

While they roast, add Soy Sauce, Sugar, Rice Vinegar and Ginger to the broth, stir until the Sugar dissolves, and add the Onions and sliced Shiitake. Simmer until the Onions are soft but still hold their shape, 15–20 min.
Whisk the Cornstarch into 100 mL cold water, stir it into the sauce and cook 2 min. Keep it loose so it soaks into the rice.

Bag in two: blast chill, then vac bag the Onion Sauce in one bag (about 4½ lbs) and the Mushrooms and Tofu together in another (about 6½ lbs). Lay flat. Label both VEGAN. Pack the Green Onion in its own deli container.

AT REXDALE: bring the Onion Sauce to a boil in a pot, fold in the Mushrooms and Tofu gently so the Tofu holds together, and reheat to 74°C (165°F). Ladle about 8½ oz over about 6 oz Plain Rice and top with Green Onion.

Add Celery, Peppers and Carrots and Sautee for another 5-10 mins, then add al pastor marinade and cook until veg is al dente
Add Cooked Portobello, and Sautee for another 5 minutes, stirring frequently
Cool in hotel pan and vac bag

recipes.notes:
Vegan pull of White Chicken & Chickpea Chili: 10 lbs come out of the same pot before the chicken goes in (its step 10), so make it alongside that recipe.
No fresh cilantro, parsley or green onion: those go into the chicken batch after the pull.
Pasta is not included. Toss about 10 oz of chili with cooked fusilli to serve.
Written 2026-11-09 for Week 4 Sunday dinner's vegan "White Chilli Pasta Casserole" (Jason: "Same pot without chicken, a pull").

ingredients.name: White Chicken & Chickpea Chili base (see recipe)

instructions: Make the White Chicken & Chickpea Chili (see that recipe) through its step 9: the beans, chickpeas, peppers, jalapeños, tomatillo salsa, lime juice, slurry and corn all go in before the chicken.
Take the 10 lbs of chili pulled before any Chicken went in (its step 10) into a clean pot or hotel pan with a clean ladle. Keep the chicken tongs, spoons and boards away from it.
Cool in the blast chiller, vac bag and label VEGAN. It travels and is stored with the regular batch, in its own bags.
To serve: reheat in the bags and toss with cooked fusilli pasta, as the chili recipe says (its step 13). About 10 oz of chili per portion.

ingredients.name: WHOLE SPICES TO BLOOM IN OIL:
Onions, rough chopped and then blitzed with immersion blender to a paste
Chopped fresh Jalapeno (seeded, blitzed lightly into the onions)

instructions: Heat oil gently in a large pot (at least 10qt)
Add whole spices and fresh ginger, garlic to oil and allow to bloom for 5-10 minutes; strain out most whole peppercorns, bay leaves, and cardamom that float to the surface and discard
Add powdered spice mix to oil and mix to combine, let bloom for another 5 minutes, then add vingear and allow to simmer for another 5 minutes, stirring to keep spices from catching
Check for seasoning and add salt/vinegar as necessary to create a rather salty/acidic solution.
Blitz the onions and jalapeno in a large, tall cambro to create a paste - a few large pieces of onion remaining is OK (use large immersion blender)
Pour spiced oil over the Onion/Japaneo mix and mix well with a paddle or large spoon to combine, simmer for 10 mins taking care not to let spices catch on the bottom of the pan
Use as a base for Vindaloo Sauce (see recipe), as well as for a base for the vegan vindaloo stew (see recipe)

recipes.kitchenNote: Batch makes about 100 lb. Rexdale is served 160 portions of 8 oz (about 80 lb); about 20 lb extra usually goes to the shelter. Don't scale the batch down to Rex's count. (Jason, 2026-11-12)

ingredients.name: White Beans, soaked overnight and cooked
Red Bell Peppers, diced (or 4 x 1.5L jars roasted peppers, chopped)
Pickled Jalapeños, lightly blitzed (1 qt container)
Cornstarch (mix with cold water for slurry)

instructions: Soak beans and chickpeas overnight. Cook until tender; reserve bean cooking water.
Cook Boneless Chicken Legs: lay on sheet pans, drizzle with oil, season with salt and pepper. Roast at 375°F until internal temp reaches 195°F. Cool and shred.
Make Tomatillo Salsa: Roast tomatillos hard until blistered. Blitz with Red Onion, Jalapeños, Parsley, and Cilantro. Season to taste.
In large pot, sauté Onions and Garlic in olive oil until very soft. Add Cumin, Paprika, Chili Powder, Granulated Onion, Granulated Garlic, Oregano, Salt, Pepper, and Bouillon. Cook 2–3 minutes.
Add Bell Peppers; sauté 5 minutes. Add Pickled Jalapeños and stir.
Add cooked white beans, chickpeas, and reserved bean water (5–10 L). Stir and simmer 20 minutes.
Add Lime Juice and Tomatillo Salsa. Stir and check seasoning.
Mix cornstarch with cold water/bean water to a slurry. Pour into simmering chili, stirring until thickened.
Add Frozen Corn. Bring back to temperature.
Reserve 10 lbs of chili (without chicken) for Vegetarian version.
Add shredded Chicken to main batch. Stir in fresh Cilantro, Parsley, and Green Onions.
Place into deep hotels and chill. Vac bag if not using within 2 days.
To serve: reheat chili in bags or hotels. Toss with cooked fusilli pasta. Each portion ~10 oz chili + pasta.
